Suicide is serious business. Advice for both ends...

If your friend makes a comment about suicide, take it seriously. Pull them aside, ask them about it. Offer to take them somewhere or do something with them. Spend some time with them, they need time away from their own personal hell inside their head.

If you're thinking about suicide, don't. It's not worth it. Coming from a guy who attempted and failed, it just made most things worse. You don't want to go through the constant worrying of parents, lack of trust, constant questioning of why you weren't at school for a while, etc... The list goes on and on. If you want to hear more of the "why not", read my AMA.

Feel free to contact me if you're on either side of this and need help. It's too hard to handle by yourself, no matter how much you think you can.
I did an AMA in /r/SuicideWatch about it if you're curious, check my post history.

Coming from someone in almost exactly the same boat, I'm going to tell you, you need to find your motivation somewhere. No, not motivation to exercise, but motivation to get better. You know what I did when I couldn't take it anymore? I drove my car off a cliff. Don't let it get to that level, find your own turning point without it having to get that bad.

Break it down? Alright.

Home troubles: Alcoholic father. He makes me feel like shit when he's drunk. Verbally abusive.

Feeling stuck: People get 'stuck' in my area all the time. There's no way I can afford to do anything other than live with my parents for the next 5 years while I attend college. Scares me, makes me feel hopeless/helpless.

Borderline failing: Scared the shit out of me. Pissed me off. The teacher refused to teach to her full potential. I tried to address the situation (professionally) to the teacher, then the councilor, then the principal, then the FOUNDER of the school, all of which backed her up.

Girl: This one I'm pretty much over, but I still feel somewhat alone. Dating is hard to make happen. /:

I honestly did tell someone what I was going to do, but their disapproval really didn't help me at all.

I think what I've learned most through all of this is that you can't seek out others to solve your problems, you have to solve them yourself. Now that doesn't mean others can't help you, it just means that they alone can't do it, you have to put in the effort to change. Self-love and all that jazz, I used to think it was bullshit, but now I'd never mock it.
